text:
jess (acct): Heads-up 1 Aurora Bank wants a targeted POC next week. Must demo Java SDK ingestion, robust streaming (SSE preferred, websocket fallback), a simple tool-call flow for fetching account metadata, and structured JSON events that their data team can consume. They also pushed a security questionnaire and want a rough monthly cost estimate.

ryan (solutions): Got it. Do we have their expected peak QPS and token profile? that drives Dedicated vs hosted suggestion.

jess (acct): They said ~150 rps sustained, spikes to 250rps; typical conversational requests ~30 tokens, but some analytics queries hit ~4k tokens. Target p95 latency under 250ms for normal flows.

mina (eng): 150-250qps with short contexts is doable on a medium Dedicated pool if we enable batching and prefix KV cache. For the 4k token backfills recommend async batch ingestion or an off-peak window to avoid cache churn. I'll prepare a concise Java streaming example and a structured event schema.

ryan (solutions): Please include a minimal tool-call sequence (tool_call -> tool_response events) we can hand to their backend team. Also note any proxy gotchas.

mina (eng): Example Java streaming snippet (very small):
```java
// minimal pseudo-code using Redwood-like client
RedwoodClient c = new RedwoodClient(System.getenv("RW_KEY"));
StreamRequest req = StreamRequest.builder()
  .model("rwd-lite-1")
  .input(userPrompt)
  .onEvent(e -> {
    // e.kind: TOKEN, TOOL_CALL, TOOL_RESPONSE, COMPLETE
    System.out.println(e.getRaw());
  })
  .build();
c.stream(req);
```
For tool calls we emit an event: {"kind":"TOOL_CALL","name":"getAccount","args":{"account_id":"..."}} and expect {"kind":"TOOL_RESPONSE","result":{...}}. Structured output example they wanted: {"type":"txn_event","ts":"...","payload":{"acct":"123","amt_cents":4500}}

mina (eng): Also note: if their L7 proxy buffers SSE chunks, streaming latency will spike. Recommend websocket fallback with a 10s heartbeat ping and chunk flush every ~1KB.

own (security): For Aurora Bank propose temporary credentials (STS) + IP allowlist. If they require tenant-controlled HSM or on-prem audit logs, escalate to Private deployment track. I can start answering the security questionnaire; flag anything that needs legal sign-off.

claire (pricing): Quick cost sketch: assume 30M tokens/month (150 rps * 30 tokens * 24*3600 ~ 39M, rounding) -> PAYG hosted approx: 39M * $0.0009 = ~$35k/mo. Committed/Dedicated: baseline pool starting ~$14k-$18k/mo depending on GPU mix; effective token price could be ~$0.0004-$0.0006 with a 6/12mo commit. We can offer a short POC credit and a capped trial rate for 30 days. I'll write a one-pager.

ryan (solutions): Integration checklist for Aurora Bank:
- Confirm L7 proxy behavior (buffering, keepalive).
- Confirm IP ranges for allowlist or plan for STS ephemeral keys.
- Validate SSE buffer sizes and recommend chunking.
- Provide WebSocket fallback example and heartbeat (10s) policy.
- Provide sample tool adapters for their metadata service.

jess (acct): They use Akamai in front and strict idle timeouts (30s). They also have an internal proxy that strips some headers.

mina (eng): Ok for Akamai we should: use websockets for long-lived streams, send periodic comments in SSE (":heartbeat\n\n") and flush, and keep messages small (<1KB) to avoid proxy coalescing. Also set client retry to fast-fail so we don't block on retries. Sample client config:
```yaml
client:
  streaming: true
  fallback: websocket
  heartbeat_seconds: 10
  retry:
    max_attempts: 2
    initial_backoff_ms: 150
```

owen (security): I'll take the sec questionnaire; expected turnaround 36 hrs for first pass. Also ensure audit export for demo is read-only. audit-bot: publishing demo audit link now.

audit-bot: Demo audit trail: https://internal.redwood/audit/aurora-poc (RO) :lock:

claire (pricing): POC offer: 14 days free up to 5M tokens, then capped billing at $5k for the remainder of month for testing. Production options will include a commit discount schedule.

ryan (solutions): One more note: Java SDK default backoff is conservative; for sub-250ms p95 tune retries and prefer fallback routing to a lighter model instead of retrying the same host. Also implement client-side request hedging for critical low-latency requests.

jess (acct): Action items: 1) Mina: Drop Java snippet + structured schema + ws fallback example in #sales-files (today). 2) Owen: Security questionnaire first pass (36h). 3) Claire: One-page cost sketch + POC credit terms (today). 4) Ryan: Integration checklist + known proxy mitigations (today). I'll run the kickoff call with Aurora tomorrow 9am PT.

mina (eng): Snippets and JSON schema uploaded to #sales-files.

claire (pricing): Sent the one-pager to Jess DM.

own (security): Uploaded questionnaire draft and flagged 2 items for product/legal.

jess (acct): Thanks team 1 I'll confirm the call and share invite. :handshake:
